# nxos_vrrpv3 (Data Source)

This data source can read the VRRPv3 (Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol version 3) configuration on NX-OS devices, including VRRPv3 interfaces, IPv4 and IPv6 groups with settings such as addresses, priority, preemption, timers and object tracking, and VRRS pathways.

### API Documentation

- [vrrpv3Entity](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:Entity/)
- [vrrpv3Inst](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:Inst/)
- [vrrpv3Interface](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:Interface/)
- [vrrpv3Vr](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:Vr/)
- [vrrpv3Addr](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:Addr/)
- [vrrpv3ObjectTrack](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:ObjectTrack/)
- [vrrpv3VrrsLeader](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:VrrsLeader/)
- [vrrpv3VrrsPathway](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:VrrsPathway/)
- [vrrpv3PwAddr](https://pubhub.devnetcloud.com/media/dme-docs-10-6-3/docs/Network%20Virtualization/vrrpv3:PwAddr/)

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "nxos_vrrpv3" "example" {
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `device` (String) A device name from the provider configuration.

### Read-Only

- `admin_state` (String) The administrative state of the object or policy.
- `id` (String) The distinguished name of the object.
- `interfaces` (Attributes Map) List of VRRPv3 interfaces.
  - Map key: `interface_id` - Must match first field in the output of `show intf brief`. Example: `eth1/1`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces))

<a id="nestedatt--interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces`

Read-Only:

- `delay_minimum` (Number) Delay in seconds, to start VRRPv3 state machine after receiving interface moving to Up state.
- `groups` (Attributes Map) List of VRRPv3 groups.
  - Map key format: `<group_id>;<address_family>`
  - Key component `group_id`: VRRPv3 Virtual Router Id. Range: `1`-`255`.
  - Key component `address_family`: Virtual Router Address Family. Choices: `ipv4`, `ipv6`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups))
- `reload_delay` (Number) Delay in seconds, to start VRRPv3 state machine after the system-reload.
- `vrrs_pathways` (Attributes Map) List of VRRS pathways.
  - Map key: `tag` - Name of vrrs tag which pathway will follow. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--vrrs_pathways))

<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.groups`

Read-Only:

- `admin_state` (String) Admin state.
- `advertisement_interval` (Number) Advertisement Interval.
- `decrement_track_priority` (Number) Priority to be decremented when tracked object is down. Default value is 10.
- `description` (String) Virtual Router Description.
- `match_address` (String) Enables matching of secondary addresses in the vrrpv3 advertisement packet against the configured vrrpv3 secondary addresses.
- `preempt` (String) Preempt.
- `preempt_delay_minimum` (Number) Miminum delay before preempt.
- `primary_address` (String) primary IP address.
- `priority` (Number) Configured Priority.
- `secondary_addresses` (Attributes Map) List of secondary addresses of the VRRPv3 group.
  - Map key: `address` - IP address. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups--secondary_addresses))
- `tracked_objects` (Attributes Map) List of objects tracked by the VRRPv3 group.
  - Map key: `id` - Object Id to be tracked.
  - Key range: `1`-`512` (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups--tracked_objects))
- `vrrpv2_compatibility_mode` (String) vrrpv2 compatibility mode.
- `vrrs_leaders` (Attributes Map) List of VRRS tags for which the VRRPv3 group is leader.
  - Map key: `tag` - VRRS tag for which group is leader. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--groups--vrrs_leaders))

<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--groups--secondary_addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.groups.secondary_addresses`


<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--groups--tracked_objects"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.groups.tracked_objects`

Read-Only:

- `decrement_priority` (Number) Priority to be decremented when tracked object is down. Default value is 10.


<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--groups--vrrs_leaders"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.groups.vrrs_leaders`



<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--vrrs_pathways"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.vrrs_pathways`

Read-Only:

- `addresses` (Attributes Map) List of addresses of the VRRS pathway.
  - Map key: `address` - IPvX address for vrrs pathway. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--interfaces--vrrs_pathways--addresses))
- `admin_state` (String) Administrative state for vrrs pathway.
- `description` (String) Description string for vrrs pathway.
- `mac_address` (String) Configured virtual MAC address for the Pathway.
- `mac_advertisement_interval` (Number) Interval in seconds, between virtual MAC unsolicited advertisements.

<a id="nestedatt--interfaces--vrrs_pathways--addresses"></a>
### Nested Schema for `interfaces.vrrs_pathways.addresses`
